stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan's landfall process begins near Odisha coast, to continue for 3 hours
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan's landfall process begins near Odisha coast, to continue for 3 hours
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan's landfall process begins near Odisha coast, to continue for 3 hours
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: According to the latest IMD update, Cyclone Akvan's outer rain bands have begun interacting with land along the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts, with the landfall process expected to commence within the next two hours.
Cyclone Akvan began making landfall along the Odisha coast on Friday morning, with the process expected to take around three hours to complete, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
The cyclone, which weakened from a severe cyclonic storm to a cyclonic storm early on Friday, is crossing the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coast close to Gopalpur.
Wind speeds of 70-80 kmph, gusting up to 90 kmph, are likely during the landfall process.
In an earlier update shared less than an hour ago, the IMD said satellite imagery showed the cyclone's outer rain bands interacting with land.

The cyclone's projected track also shifted over the past 24 hours, with the likely landfall zone moving towards the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coast from earlier projections that pointed to Andhra Pradesh, bringing southern Odisha into the focus of the storm's impact.
The Odisha government has stepped up evacuation and relief operations across vulnerable districts as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast.
More than 3 lakh people have been evacuated and shifted to 2,523 relief camps, while 423 rescue teams have been deployed to deal with any emergency.

The state has also identified 9,341 cyclone shelters across potentially affected districts, with arrangements for cooked and dry food, drinking water, essential medicines, sanitary napkins and other necessities, including facilities for children.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has reviewed the preparations and reiterated the government's commitment to its zero-casualty mission.
The emergency response includes 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 131 Fire and Emergency Services teams.
The Indian Coast Guard has also been asked to keep its helicopters, vessels and other logistical support ready for rescue and relief operations.

stories.headline: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
stories.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
stories.summary: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Several districts in the southern part of West Bengal, including Kolkata, will receive heavy rainfall until November 21 due to the cyclonic storm Akvan.

The storm, which lay over the east-central Bay of Bengal on Thursday morning (November 19, 2026), is expected to make landfall around noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), along the coast between Narsipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Puri (Odisha), close to Gopalpur.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a warning of heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds in Kolkata, North 24 Parganas, Howrah, Hooghly, and Purulia districts, while South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, and Bankura are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.
Since Wednesday night (November 18, 2026), Kolkata and several other south Bengal districts have experienced overnight and morning rainfall under the influence of the weather system.
The intensity of rain in Kolkata increased as the day progressed after the city woke up to a drizzle on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

Squally wind speeds of 40–50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are also likely to prevail along and off the West Bengal coast until Friday noon and decrease thereafter, while sea conditions will remain very rough, said IMD.
The IMD also advised fishermen not to venture into the deep sea toward the Northwest and West-Central Bay of Bengal until Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The South Eastern Railway has cancelled about 19 trains on November 19 and 20 due to the possible impact of the cyclone.
“We are prepared for any unprecedented situation.
Our workers and officers are all at alert.
If there is any waterlogging, we will pump it out with motors.

We are coordinating with other departments and doing this as teamwork, including the power department, port authorities, disaster management, PWD, and others,” Minister of Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Agnimitra Paul said.

stories.headline: China, Russia, US agree on nuclear risk reduction, energy security in joint declaration
stories.title: China, Russia, US agree on nuclear risk reduction, energy security in joint declaration
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 19: China, Russia, and the United States on Thursday issued a joint declaration titled Declaration toward Peace following an unprecedented trilateral meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen. The declaration said the three leaders were committed to upholding strategic stability and international security, and agreed that “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought”. They also agreed to continue dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. The statement outlined cooperation on energy security, with the three countries planning to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all countries. On international legal principles, the leaders underlined the importance of state consent and immunity enjoyed by state officials. They also agreed that the International Criminal Court and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction. The three countries, all permanent members of the UN Security Council, also expressed their commitment to reforming the United Nations to make it more effective in addressing global challenges and maintaining international peace and security. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the two-day Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, which brought together leaders and representatives of 21 member economies.
